propositions: The tickets branch is 1.04 GiB, with 92% consumed by the reconciler's .bridge_state cache; growth is driven by bookkeeping fields baseline_advanced_at (1144 changes per pass, read nowhere) and last_get_pass (20 rotations per pass) that defeat git delta compression.

Marginal packed cost per committed bindings.json version is 12.79 KB today; deleting baseline_advanced_at reduces it to 1.74 KB (7.4x improvement) and moving last_get_pass out of the file halves version count (12.8x total improvement).

The reconciler runs on ephemeral GitHub runners and requires durable .bridge_state in git; the solution keeps the cache on-branch but makes it cheap by removing unnecessary timestamp and rotation bookkeeping fields.

A one-time history rewrite using git fast-export/filter/fast-import reduces the tickets branch from 1.17 GB to 98.8 MB (8.4% of original) while preserving all commits, merges, and producing byte-identical HEAD tree after dynamic re-add.

Post-rewrite writer clones must detect and refuse epoch mismatches at both sync._union_merge and push.py sites; rollback is via operator-controlled force ref replacement to the old tip preserved in an off-repo backup bundle.

The rollout requires quiescence gates: A2-2 gated by descendant workflow execution plus explicit host refresh; reclaim gated by epoch-refusal proofs from live review-bot and host runtimes, verified off-repo bundle, and operator confirmation of zero sessions and stopped rebar-mcp servers.
